text:
Predicates:
Employee(x) ::: x is an employee.
SchedulesMeeting(x, y) ::: x schedules a meeting with y.
AppearsToday(x) ::: x appears in the company today.
LunchInCompany(x) ::: x has lunch in the company.
LunchAtHome(x) ::: x has lunch at home.
WorkingRemotelyFromHome(x) ::: x works remotely from home.
InOtherCountry(x) ::: x is in another country.
Manager(x) ::: x is a manager.
James ::: James
Premises:
∀x (SchedulesMeeting(x, y) → AppearsToday(x)) ::: All employees who schedule a meeting with their customers will appear in the company today.
∀x (LunchInCompany(x) → SchedulesMeeting(x, y)) ::: Everyone who has lunch in the company schedules meetings with their customers.
∀x (LunchInCompany(x) ∨ LunchAtHome(x)) ::: Employees will either have lunch in the company or at home.
∀x (LunchAtHome(x) → WorkingRemotelyFromHome(x)) ::: If an employee has lunch at home, then he/she is working remotely from home.
∀x (InOtherCountry(x) → WorkingRemotelyFromHome(x)) ::: All employees who are in other countries work remotely from home.
∀x (Manager(x) → ¬WorkingRemotelyFromHome(x)) ::: No managers work remotely from home.
(Manager(James) ∧ AppearsToday(James)) ∨ (¬Manager(James) ∧ ¬AppearsToday(James)) ::: James is either a manager and appears in the company today or neither a manager nor appears in the company today.
Conclusion:
¬LunchInCompany(James) ::: James does not have lunch in the company.
